routes.description: Establish that natural science is a powerful but domain-limited mode of inquiry and that rational explanation also includes agency, purpose, normativity, historical inference, and an account of why an intelligible universe is accessible to rational minds.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one significant question worth explaining cannot be resolved by scientific mechanism alone and a distinct form of explanation is shown to be rationally applicable rather than merely filling a temporary empirical gap.

motionBridge.description: Show that explanations worth having are not exhausted by publicly testable natural mechanisms and that at least one additional explanatory category is rationally required.

centralBridges.description: Distinguish scientific descriptions of natural processes from explanations involving agency, purpose, meaning, or obligation.
Account for the rational intelligibility of nature and the reliability of minds that investigate it without presupposing that scientific method explains its own foundations.
Establish that claims about divine action, cosmic origin, or historically alleged miracles can be assessed through rational and evidential inquiry rather than excluded by definition.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how affirming natural regularities and scientific progress remains compatible with deeper purposive or agent-based explanation.
Connect the proposed wider explanatory framework to moral responsibility, human significance, and personal meaning.

routes.description: Establish science as the uniquely reliable route to reality, argue that its progressive natural explanations face no demonstrated terminal boundary, and show that purported alternatives either lack public evidence or project human concerns beyond what reality warrants.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if scientific inquiry can in principle cover every genuine evidential question while purpose, supernatural agency, objective normativity, and related alleged exceptions are either naturally explainable or not warranted as features requiring explanation.

motionBridge.description: Show that every genuine question about reality is in principle answerable through evidence-governed scientific inquiry, with no established need for another explanatory kind.

centralBridges.description: Defend public evidence, testability, and mutually supporting natural explanations as the criteria for legitimate claims about reality.
Provide or motivate impersonal natural accounts of cosmic order, origins, cognition, life, and moral behavior without invoking divine agency.
Show that supernatural and purposive proposals do not add warranted explanatory content beyond natural inquiry.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use the continuing reach and precision of scientific progress to support confidence in eventual explanatory completeness.
Distinguish evidential questions about reality from projected human desires for cosmic purpose or permanent significance.

sections.title: The Scope and Standards of Rational Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue sets the motion-level framework by testing whether scientific evidence and mechanism exhaust legitimate explanation or coexist with irreducible explanations involving agents, purposes, and other rational categories.

sections.title: Scientific Progress, Intelligibility, and Rational Minds
sections.rationale: The competing accounts must explain both science's expanding success and the preconditions that make an orderly world knowable by evolved human cognition, including whether those preconditions support naturalism or a deeper source.

sections.title: Origins of Natural Law, the Universe, and Life
sections.rationale: Cosmic lawfulness, the emergence of a universe, and the boundary between prebiotic origins and biological evolution provide direct tests of whether natural explanation is sufficient in principle or leaves a foundational remainder.

sections.title: Miracles, Historical Evidence, and Revisability
sections.rationale: The resurrection dispute concentrates the clash over natural regularity, historical testimony, exceptional agency, and what observations could rationally revise either supernatural belief or disbelief.

sections.title: Morality, Purpose, and Human Meaning
sections.rationale: Moral obligation, shared values, cosmic purpose, and human significance test whether scientific and evolutionary accounts explain all relevant phenomena or only describe facts and behavior without grounding normativity or meaning.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Natural science does not answer every meaningful question, and mechanistic explanations can coexist with rational explanations involving agency and purpose.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Scientific laws describe the regular behavior of nature but cannot exclude a resurrection caused by exceptional divine agency.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: If human cognition is the product of a mindless unguided process, trust in the rational faculties required for science is undermined, whereas theism supplies a basis for that trust.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Belief in one rational creator supported the emergence of modern science and forms part of a cumulative explanation for the fit between an intelligible universe and the human mind.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: The universe came from no physical material but not from absolute nothing, because nonphysical divine mind is its creative source, a view compatible with a cosmic beginning.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Christian belief is in principle revisable through historical counterexplanations and defeaters of attributed experiences, while its cumulative evidential support warrants continued commitment and scrutiny.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Science can describe moral behavior and consequences, but natural laws and evolutionary accounts do not themselves generate prescriptive duties or provide a scientific foundation for ethics.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Cross-cultural agreement on a core of moral judgments is explained by human beings having been created as morally responsible persons in the image of God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Natural selection cannot explain the origin of life because evolutionary mechanisms can operate only after living systems already exist.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Science can ultimately explain every genuine question because publicly testable evidence and mutually supporting scientific ideas disclose reality without an evident terminal barrier.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The resurrection should be rejected because late religious testimony is not credible evidence and the physical decay of a dead body makes natural reconstitution impossible.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Attributing events to an unrestricted divine agent does not genuinely explain them because it replaces investigation of underlying biological, chemical, physical, and mathematical processes.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Evolution can produce brains capable of extraordinary scientific understanding, while mathematical prediction can remain precise even where human intuition reaches its limits.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Cosmic purpose is not an evidential question because it projects temporary human purposes onto the universe without evidence that the universe has a corresponding ultimate purpose.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: The laws of nature can be accounted for through the impersonal principles of indolence, anarchy, and ignorance without positing a divine agent behind them.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: A universe can arise from nothing through the separation of balanced opposites, with total charge and energy summing to zero and scientific inquiry progressively narrowing the remaining origin problem.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Even directly witnessing an apparent resurrection would not establish divine intervention because hallucination would remain more credible than a supernatural explanation.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Morality can be explained as evolved behavioral infrastructure supplemented by the distinctively human capacity to contemplate the consequences of actions.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: As science advances, its expanding natural explanations progressively eliminate the need to invoke supernatural causes.
